title: Baker's 114 Rewrites the Record Book as Patterson Surges
title_candidates: Baker's 114 Rewrites the Record Book as Patterson Surges
New Course Worst Overshadows a Tidy Trophy Charge
A Record Collapse and a Quiet Rise at Praia D'El Rey
theme: A record-breaking collapse dominates a round otherwise defined by John Patterson's early Trophy surge.
opening_hook: Round one at Praia D'El Rey produced a leaderboard nobody will remember and a number nobody will forget: 114, the worst round the course has ever hosted.

round_story.subject: John Patterson's round survives two early quadruple bogeys to become the best score of the day
round_story.why_it_matters: It is the best Stableford return of the round and hands Patterson the outright TEG 17 Trophy lead going into round two.
round_story.shape: Two quadruple bogeys inside the first six holes threaten to wreck Patterson's day, but a birdie at the 12th arrests the slide and two shot-free stretches down the closing holes carry him to 39 points, the best of the field, and an outright Trophy lead grabbed at the 16th.
headline_candidates: Patterson's Late Surge Tops the Field
Patterson Recovers to Lead the Way
round_story.chosen_headline: Patterson's Late Surge Tops the Field
round_story.standfirst: A day that began with back-to-back quadruple bogeys ended with the best score of the round and an outright grip on the TEG 17 Trophy.

race_story.subject: The early state of all three races after one round at Praia D'El Rey
race_story.why_it_matters: With no prior rounds to measure against, this round alone sets the shape of the TEG 17 Trophy, Green Jacket and Wooden Spoon tables heading into day two.
race_story.shape: Jon Baker held the outright Trophy lead as early as the 3rd before Patterson overtook him late; Gregg Williams drew level with Jon Baker for the TEG 17 Green Jacket lead at the 17th; and Alex Baker's horror show leaves him already marooned at the bottom of the TEG 17 Wooden Spoon table by a single point.
headline_candidates: Early Lead Changes Set the Tone
race_story.standfirst: One round in, the Green Jacket is already a two-way tie and the Wooden Spoon has found its first occupant.

discovered_storylines.subject: Alex Baker shatters the Praia D'El Rey course record with a 114
discovered_storylines.why_it_matters: It is a new course worst by four shots across 24 prior visits, the single most extreme number of the day, and effectively pre-decides the Wooden Spoon and Green Jacket races before round two.
discovered_storylines.shape: A sextuple bogey at the 5th anchors a stretch that bleeds 13 shots in three holes, compounded by a quadruple bogey at the 4th and a closing quintuple bogey at the 18th; the round totals 114 gross, a new course worst and 14 shots worse than his own previous best here.
headline_candidates: Baker Rewrites the Record Books, Badly
A New Worst at Praia D'El Rey
discovered_storylines.chosen_headline: Baker Rewrites the Record Books, Badly
discovered_storylines.standfirst: Five ruinous holes and a closing quintuple bogey leave the course record broken for all the wrong reasons.

discovered_storylines.subject: David Mullin's round splits neatly into a horror front nine and a big finish
discovered_storylines.why_it_matters: His 33-point Trophy return hides a stark front-to-back split worth flagging as the shape of his whole round.
discovered_storylines.shape: Mullin drops 11 shots across holes 4 to 8, including a triple bogey at the 8th, before reeling off 16 Stableford points across holes 12 to 16 with a birdie at the 13th, turning a bleak morning into a genuine two-act round.
headline_candidates: From Disaster to Recovery in Nine Holes
Mullin Fights Back After the Turn
discovered_storylines.standfirst: A front nine that threatened to unravel gave way to the best stretch of anyone's day.

race_state_note: With no prior rounds banked, round one alone establishes all three competition tables.
